text:
Arseny Gritsyuk was a fifth-round pick in 2019 who spent three more seasons in the KHL before trying the NHL. Year two in New Jersey has turned him into a talking point: eight goals in 16 games, tied with Jack Hughes for the team lead, after 13 in all of last season. Yahoo Sports is already asking whether he can keep up the pace, which is the right question.

Our answer is partly. He is getting better looks than last year, close to a goal of expected value per 60 minutes, and the Devils control play when he is on (a 64% share of the 5v5 chances). That is a real middle-six winger on a line that is working. But he has scored eight on about four goals' worth of chances, shooting 21% after 9% a year ago, and his linemates are converting well above their chances too. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had more than half his shots coming off the rush last season, so he lives in transition. Expect the goals to slow; our projection still lands him in the high 20s, a very good year for a 129th pick.
headline: Gritsyuk's scoring pace and the honest forecast
